code_snippet: query = "SELECT id, username, password_hash, role FROM users WHERE username = '" + username + "'"
vulnerability_description: User input concatenated into SQL query
attack_scenario: Submit ' OR '1'='1' -- as username to bypass authentication or exfiltrate the users table

vulnerability_description: Production database password and API key committed to source control
attack_scenario: Anyone with repository access reads credentials directly from git history
remediation: Load from environment variables; rotate exposed credentials

attack_scenario: POST a crafted pickle payload to /import_schedule to execute arbitrary code on the server
remediation: Use JSON (json.loads) or a signed/deserialization-safe format

vulnerability_description: Authenticated users can read every appointment regardless of role
attack_scenario: Any authenticated low-privileged user calls /appointments and reads all patient schedules
remediation: Enforce role check (e.g. require_role('physician')) and scope query to the user's patients

vulnerability_description: User-controlled filename joined into filesystem path
attack_scenario: Request filename=../../etc/passwd to read arbitrary server files
remediation: Reject path separators; validate with os.path.basename and a whitelist directory check

vulnerability_description: Unsalted SHA-1 used for password verification
attack_scenario: Attackers crack SHA-1 hashes at billions of guesses/sec with commodity GPUs
remediation: Use bcrypt (or argon2id) with per-user salt

vulnerability_description: Raw exception, stack trace, and DB password returned in HTTP response
attack_scenario: Trigger any exception to harvest stack details and the database password from the response
remediation: Return a generic error message; log details server-side only

vulnerability_description: User-controlled redirect target without allowlist validation
attack_scenario: Send victims a link like /redirect?url=https://evil.example to phish credentials
remediation: Validate target against an allowlist of trusted URLs or use relative paths only
